Where to Stay in Sing Buri?
12 Hotels We Actually Reviewed
Prices Compared Across 3 Sites!
heroSub: 12 hand-picked Sing Buri hotels across every budget — a hotel on the Chao Phraya River in town, a pool boutique villa, a rice-field resort in Bang Rachan and a 9.4-rated countryside homestay. Covering the town centre, Phrom Buri and Bang Rachan. From roughly ฿400–1,200/night.
introH2: 🏞️ Why does choosing the right area in Sing Buri matter?
introHtml: Sing Buri is a small town on the Asia Highway that many people stop in for a single night on the way north — but it actually has sights spread across several areas. Stays fall into three sides with different feels — the town centre of Sing Buri has the Chao Phraya riverfront, Wat Phra Non Chaksi, the FN Outlet and markets, ideal if you want to be near the food and the main sights; Phrom Buri district sits to the south along the Asia Highway, handy for a stopover or a quieter base; and Bang Rachan district to the west is home to the Bang Rachan Heroes Monument, Wat Pho Kao Ton and a rural rice-field feel. Many people book without checking the area and end up driving back and forth all day. This guide rounds up 12 hand-picked Sing Buri hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Sing Buri has no metro, no airport and no railway station in the town itself — most people arrive by car or by van/coach to the bus terminal, so having your own car is easiest. Pick by your itinerary: the town centre (Bang Man·Ton Pho·Chaksi) is near the Chao Phraya riverfront, Wat Phra Non Chaksi, the FN Outlet and the markets, best if you want to be central; Phrom Buri sits on the Asia Highway to the south, good for a stopover and a quieter stay; and Bang Rachan (Mae La·Phochonkai) lets you visit the Bang Rachan camp, Wat Pho Kao Ton and stay amid the rural rice fields. Almost every hotel has free parking, so they suit self-drivers well.

entries.name: Chaisaeng Palace Hotel
entries.revCount: 214 reviews · most in this guide · river views
entries.badge: 🏆 Most reviewed 214 · on the Chao Phraya
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Wilaichit Rd · Bang Man · town centre
entries.addr: 982/9 Wilaichit Rd, Bang Man, Mueang Sing Buri
entries.storyHtml: Chaisaeng Palace is the most reviewed hotel in this guide, with 214 reviews, and the 4-star that balances a solid score with a deep review base best, scoring 8.6. The point guests agree on is that most rooms face the Chao Phraya River, with lovely views from inside. It sits in the town centre in Bang Man, near the FN Outlet and the provincial hall, with free parking and a shuttle — good for both a stopover and exploring the province.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request a river-view room when booking, and if you're sensitive to noise pick a higher floor, since the restaurant downstairs has music until around 11pm on some nights.
pros: Most rooms have Chao Phraya River views — the standout guests agree on
Most reviews in the guide (214) — solid data
Central location near the FN Outlet and provincial hall
Free parking, shuttle service, friendly staff
cons: Music from the downstairs restaurant carries until about 11pm some nights
No swimming pool, and some decor is starting to show its age

entries.name: Sing Buri Homestay
entries.revCount: 31 reviews · highest score in this guide 9.4
entries.addr: 68 Soi Sukhaphiban Sing Buri 14, Phochonkai, Bang Rachan
entries.storyHtml: Sing Buri Homestay is the highest-scoring stay in this guide at 9.4 from 31 reviews, a family homestay many guests say feels like visiting a friend's house. The draw is the warm hosts and home-cooked Thai food made fresh every meal. It's in Phochonkai, Bang Rachan, with a quiet rural feel and bicycles to ride around the village — great for a real rest and a taste of countryside life, though you'll need your own car.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: There are very few rooms, so book ahead, and tell the hosts in advance if you want a made-to-order breakfast so they can prepare fresh ingredients.
pros: Highest score in the guide, 9.4 from 31 reviews
Warm hosts; tasty home-cooked food made fresh
Quiet rural setting — a genuine rest
Bicycles to rent, free parking and airport transfer
cons: Rural location far from town — you'll need your own car
Very few rooms, so book ahead · made-to-order breakfast costs extra

entries.name: Chaisaeng Villa Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ton Pho · Bang Phutsa · town centre
entries.addr: 11 Moo 1, Ton Pho, Mueang Sing Buri
entries.storyHtml: Chaisaeng Villa is a 4-star boutique hotel that looks new and earns a high 9.1 on Agoda. The point guests agree on is spacious, clean rooms with comfy beds that feel good value for a 4-star. It's in Ton Pho in the town centre, near the Chao Phraya River and the provincial hall, with a lobby and a pleasant beer garden, plus free parking — good for both leisure and business. The review base is still small, but the feedback is steadily positive.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget allows, take the larger VIP Room — some have a balcony. If you're noise-sensitive, check whether there's an event on at the beer garden that night.
pros: Looks new and clean; 9.1 on Agoda
Spacious rooms, comfy beds, good 4-star value
Central location near the river and provincial hall
Pleasant beer garden, free parking
cons: Not in a walkable shopping street — you'll need a car
Some evenings have outdoor music/events, which can be noisy

entries.name: Golden Dragon Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ton Pho · near the Chao Phraya · in town
entries.addr: 71 Moo 11, Bang Rachan Tat Mai Rd, Ton Pho, Mueang Sing Buri
entries.storyHtml: Golden Dragon Resort is an in-town resort that scores a high 9.1 from 43 reviews at a starting price of just ฿580. What guests praise most is the varied breakfast that many say is better than the room price suggests, plus rooms of about 28 sqm with soft beds and strong water pressure. It's in Ton Pho near the Chao Phraya River and the town, with easy parking — good for anyone after a spacious room and a good breakfast on a budget.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a higher floor or a room away from the downstairs restaurant on nights with functions, and head down to breakfast early while everything is still stocked.
pros: 9.1 score from 43 reviews, starting at just ฿580
Varied breakfast — many say it beats the room price
Spacious rooms ~28 sqm, soft beds, strong water pressure
In-town near the river and markets; easy parking
cons: The downstairs restaurant carries noise to the rooms some nights
Cleanliness and Wi-Fi can be inconsistent in some rooms

entries.name: Central Park Hotel
entries.revCount: 150 reviews · large review base · good value
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Man · near markets & FN Outlet · in town
entries.addr: 172/2 Moo 1, Bang Man, Mueang Sing Buri
entries.storyHtml: Central Park Hotel is a budget in-town hotel with a large base of 150 reviews, and many guests say it punches above its 3-star price, scoring 8.5. The strengths are rooms larger than expected, cold air-con, a separate wet/dry bathroom and balconies in many rooms. It's in Bang Man in the town centre, near markets, the provincial hall and the FN Outlet, with free parking and free Wi-Fi — good for anyone after a good-value central room.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pin the map before you go — the entrance is hard to find and the sign is unclear, so many people drive past. There's no breakfast, so plan to eat at the nearby market.
pros: Punches above its 3-star price; rooms bigger than expected
Large review base of 150 — solid data
Separate wet/dry bathroom; balconies in many rooms
Central, near markets and the FN Outlet; free parking
cons: Entrance is hard to find with an unclear sign — pin the map
No breakfast and no swimming pool

entries.name: Sumali Villa
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chaksi · near Wat Phra Non Chaksi · outskirts
entries.storyHtml: Sumali Villa is a 4-star boutique villa of just four rooms, set in the Thai-French owners' architect-designed house with a pool in the garden, scoring 8.4. What guests praise most is the fresh-made breakfast that many call the best of their trip, plus a quiet, private feel. It's in Chaksi near Wat Phra Non Chaksi — great for anyone wanting a stay with character to relax in, though you'll need a car as there's nothing walkable nearby.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Pin the map carefully, as the entrance sign is unclear and first-timers get lost. It's a real family home, so guests share the communal pool and garden.
pros: Boutique villa with a garden pool — quiet and private
Fresh-made breakfast many call the best of their trip
Spacious, clean rooms with a balcony and sitting sofa
Thai-French owners host in person and suggest things to do
cons: Out of town with nothing walkable nearby — you'll need a car
Entrance sign is unclear · guests share the communal pool and garden

entries.name: Rim Thung Mae La Resort
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Mae La · Bang Rachan · in the rice fields
entries.addr: 37/4 Moo 1, Mae La, Bang Rachan district
entries.storyHtml: Rim Thung Mae La is a small new-build resort in the Bang Rachan rice fields that scores 8.6, and as high as 9.0 on Agoda. The draw is a brand-new, very clean building with balconies looking over the fields and gardens, and a quiet that feels cut off from the bustle. It's great for resting in nature and photographing the rice views, but with only about four rooms you need to book ahead, and it sits in a rural village where you'll drive out to find food. The review base is still small, so we rank it cautiously.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Book several days ahead, as there are very few rooms, and pack some snacks in the car since there's nothing walkable nearby.
pros: New building, very clean, quiet in the rice fields
Rooms have a balcony with rice-field/garden views
8.6 score (up to 9.0 on Agoda); friendly owners
Free private parking — good for self-drivers
cons: Only about four rooms — book ahead
Rural village with nothing walkable nearby · small review base

entries.name: Je t'aime Cafe & Villa
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Pho Kruam · near town · near the city pillar shrine
entries.storyHtml: Je t'aime Cafe & Villa is a small cafe boutique villa with a deep base of 101 reviews despite being a 2-star, scoring 8.1. The selling point is a pretty European cafe setting with plenty of photo corners, plus an outdoor pool and poolside bar in a small property, and themed rooms suited to couples. It's in Pho Kruam near the town and the city pillar shrine, with breakfast included — great for couples wanting a stay with character.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: With only about six rooms it fills up easily on weekends, so book ahead, and treat it as a small cafe villa rather than a full-service hotel.
pros: Pretty European cafe setting with many photo corners
Outdoor pool and poolside bar
Cute themed rooms for couples; breakfast included
Lots of reviews (101) · near town, free parking
cons: Only about six rooms — fills up easily on weekends
A small villa — fewer services than a full hotel

entries.name: Zen Garden Resort
entries.revCount: 10 reviews · on the Asia Highway · newish rooms
entries.badge: 🛣️ On the Asia Highway, easy stopover
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Man · on the Asia Highway · Mueang Sing Buri

entries.addr: 142 Moo 1, Asia Highway, Bang Man, Mueang Sing Buri
entries.storyHtml: Zen Garden Resort is a fairly new roadside resort on the Asia Highway, ideal as a stopover, scoring 8.2. The strengths are spacious, clean rooms with a comfy 6-foot bed and an easy-to-find location right on the main road, with a wide concrete lot that's easy to park in. It has a smart TV with streaming apps and free Wi-Fi — good for self-drivers passing through who want a good-value room and easy parking, though the review base is still small.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The building has no lift, so ask for a ground-floor room if you have heavy bags, and be prepared for fairly weak water pressure.

entries.name: Baanbudsarin Apartment
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Man · near Lotus's · Mueang Sing Buri
entries.addr: 190/39 Moo 7, Bang Man, Mueang Sing Buri
entries.storyHtml: Baanbudsarin Apartment is the cheapest stay in this guide, starting at just ฿400, with a large base of 90 reviews, scoring 8.1. The strength is a very light price for budget travellers, with balconies and a sitting area in many rooms, air-con, a fridge and 24-hour reception. It's in Bang Man in town, near Lotus's and restaurants where food is easy to find, with free parking — good for backpackers and overnight stops, though the building is aging, so check the latest photos before booking.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Room condition varies, so check the latest photos and reviews before booking, and pick a room with a balcony for a bit more private space for just ฿50 more.
pros: Cheapest in the guide at ฿400 — good value on a budget
Large base of 90 reviews · balconies in many rooms
In town near Lotus's and restaurants — easy to find food
Free parking, 24-hour reception, laundry machines

Inconsistent cleanliness · no breakfast and no pool

entries.name: Parida Resort
entries.badge: 👨‍👩‍👧 Big family room · water play for kids
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ban Mo · Phrom Buri · on the Asia Highway
entries.addr: 142 Moo 4, Ban Mo, Phrom Buri district
entries.storyHtml: Parida Resort is a small, quiet resort in Phrom Buri suited to families and stopovers, scoring 7.2. The strengths are a very large family room of about 50 sqm — a lot of space for the price — a shady garden setting and a small water-play feature kids enjoy. It's in Ban Mo right on the Asia Highway, but about 20 km from central Sing Buri so you'll need to drive, and there's nothing walkable nearby. The review base is still small, so we rank it cautiously.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Travelling as a family, take the very spacious Queen Family Room, and pack food in the car, as there are no shops nearby and no in-house restaurant.
pros: Very large family room ~50 sqm at a modest price
Quiet, shady garden — a relaxed, low-key stay
Small water-play feature kids enjoy
Free private parking — good for self-drivers

Small resort with no in-house restaurant · small review base

entries.name: Grand Leo Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Bang Man · near Wat Pho Ngoen · town centre
entries.addr: 198 Moo 7, Bang Man, Mueang Sing Buri
entries.storyHtml: Grand Leo Hotel closes the guide as a cheap central option for anyone who just wants a one-night stop. The good parts are a central location within walking distance of the city pillar shrine and Wat Pho Ngoen, fairly spacious rooms with a balcony and fridge, and free parking. But to be straight with you, the overall score is 5.6 from 10 reviews — some reviews report inconsistent cleanliness and upkeep — so we place it last for honesty's sake. It suits only those who genuinely prioritise price and location.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Confirm the rate and room type in advance, as some reviews mention the counter price not matching the booking, and ask to see the room first if you can.
pros: Central — walk to the city pillar shrine and Wat Pho Ngoen
Fairly spacious rooms with a balcony and fridge
Cheap from ฿500 · free parking and free Wi-Fi

faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Sing Buri hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Sing Buri?
faq.a: It depends on your plans. The town centre (Bang Man·Ton Pho·Chaksi) suits those who want to be near the Chao Phraya riverfront, Wat Phra Non Chaksi, the FN Outlet and markets (Chaisaeng Palace, Chaisaeng Villa, Golden Dragon, Central Park). Phrom Buri sits on the Asia Highway to the south, good for a stopover (Parida Resort). Bang Rachan suits visiting the Bang Rachan camp and staying amid the rice fields (Sing Buri Homestay, Rim Thung Mae La).

faq.q: ❓ How much do Sing Buri hotels cost?
faq.a: Prices are lighter than in many provinces: budget apartments and hotels start around ฿400–700 a night; resorts and midrange-to-4-star hotels run about ฿700–1,000; pool boutique villas and breakfast-included stays run about ฿1,079–1,200. Almost all have free parking.

faq.q: ❓ Which Sing Buri stay has the best review scores?
faq.a: From what we've gathered, Sing Buri Homestay scores highest at 9.4 (a Bang Rachan homestay with great home cooking), followed by Chaisaeng Villa and Golden Dragon Resort at 9.1. The one with the largest review base is Chaisaeng Palace, with 214 reviews and an 8.6 score, with Chao Phraya river-view rooms.

faq.q: ❓ Are there Sing Buri hotels with a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes, but not many — Sumali Villa ฿1,200 is a boutique villa with a garden pool, and Je t'aime Cafe & Villa ฿1,079 has an outdoor pool with a poolside bar. Most in-town hotels have no pool, so if a pool matters, those two are the picks.

faq.q: ❓ Can I visit Sing Buri without my own car?
faq.a: Sing Buri has no metro, no airport and no railway station in town; most people arrive by van or coach to the bus terminal. Without a car, pick a town-centre stay (such as Chaisaeng Palace or Central Park) near the markets and restaurants and use local hired transport. The Bang Rachan homestay and out-of-town resorts really need a car.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Sing Buri hotel?
faq.a: For ordinary weekdays, booking 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. But the few-room stays — the homestay, boutique villas and the rice-field resort (Sing Buri Homestay, Sumali Villa, Rim Thung Mae La, Je t'aime) — fill up fast on long weekends and holidays, so book several days to a month ahead.
